extracted.intended_audience: scientists and researchers; readers and potential authors of the "Citation Classics" column; Current Contents audience
extracted.subtask_description: Producing/Selecting author commentaries and digests for highly-cited papers (the "Citation Classics" column): choosing candidate papers by citation frequency and commissioning retrospectives that explain significance and context for a general scientific readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection from the 500 most-cited papers (1961-1972)
rubrics_metrics.description: The candidates for Citation Classics will be selected from a group 500 papers most cited during the years 1961-1972.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection is explicitly based on citation frequency during the specified interval; many candidates have been listed previously in Current Contents. The pool therefore emphasizes papers with demonstrated high citation counts within that time window, regardless of original publication date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highly cited status / 'classic' citation thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers in this group include some of the most cited papers ever published — the feature targets the most highly-cited works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The column treats extreme citation frequency as the primary signal of 'classic' status (example given: Lowry’s paper has accumulated more citations than the next six combined). Implicitly, being among the top-cited papers historically or within the period confers candidacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author-authored retrospective commentary explaining significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Citation Classic will include a commentary by the author explaining why the paper proved to be so important.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commentary should be retrospective (looking back) and written by the original author where possible. It should address the reasons for the paper’s impact, and serve as the author's personal account of the work's significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a synopsis or digest for non-specialist readers
rubrics_metrics.description: For each paper we will provide a synopsis or digest so readers who are unfamiliar with the field can better appreciate its significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The digest must summarize key points of the work at an accessible level, enabling readers outside the specialty to grasp the paper’s contribution; clarity and concision are implied priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discuss human-side aspects and development of the work
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors will discuss interesting aspects of their work retrospectively — techniques, the development of the work, the role played by coauthors or others, and encouragement received from colleagues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize the human/history angle: anecdotes, personal recollections, collaborations, and influences are encouraged. The column highlights 'the human side of science' and values narrative elements (surprises, delight, serendipity) alongside technical discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge citation accrual timelines and publication dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Many papers selected were published in earlier decades (1940s–1960s) yet achieved highest citation rates years later; selection uses citation frequency within the defined period rather than publication recency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When presenting a classic, note its publication date and the timeline of its citations (e.g., peak citation years may occur many years after publication). This guards against conflating age with impact and explains why older papers appear among modern 'most-cited' lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feature formatting: combine author commentary with editorial context
rubrics_metrics.description: The new feature will include both the author’s commentary and editorial syntheses (e.g., lists, rankings, editorial notes) to place the paper in the context of citation-frequency rankings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect each entry to pair an author’s retrospective with editorial material such as rank-order lists or brief notes about the paper's standing among all-time most-cited works; the column may publish ranked lists (e.g., fifty most cited papers) alongside individual commentaries.
